sources.title: Bertold Spuler: Central Asia in the Mongol and Timurid periods
sources.note: Direct institutional PDF read, pages 1 to 4: geography, inherited ulus, administration and seasonal residences. Old generalized value judgments and claim of Iranian-language disappearance are not adopted. Imported outline independently decoded.

sources.title: Peter Jackson: Chaghatayid dynasty, history
sources.note: Direct institutional PDF read. Pages 1 to 2 inheritance and fiscal independence under Alghu; pages 6 to 7 western/eastern division, Timur, eastern succession and 1514 Kashgar state. Older Tarmashirin reign dates superseded by Biran for that passage.

sources.title: Abdulkadir Yuvali: Chagatai Khanate
sources.note: Direct scholarly Turkish entry read. Ergene regency, Talas 1269 agreement about summer/winter pastures and cultivated land, Kebek silver coinage. No adoption of older disputed precise accession dates.

sources.title: Michal Biran: The Chaghadaids and Islam, Tarmashirin Khan
sources.note: Author-uploaded full scholarly text read. Journal of the American Oriental Society 122.4 (2002), pages 742 to 752, DOI 10.2307/3217613. Pages 745 to 747 reign revised to 1331 to 1334 and conversion/social context; pages 750 to 751 earlier Muslim khans.

sources.title: Daniel Waugh, University of Washington: Almaliq
sources.note: Direct university field-history page read. Chang Chun 1221 quotations explicitly formation-era background; cotton/fruit/canals. Last architectural paragraphs distinguish uncertain tomb date and Tini Khatun patronage. 2005 hospitality not back-projected.

sources.title: Azret Sultan Museum: Coin hoards in the museum collections
sources.note: Indexed original museum Russian text read: hoard 2, Kultobe excavations 1980 to 1982; original 202 silver and 87 copper, only 24 silver and two copper transferred to museum for unknown reasons. Mint list retained; collection subset is not entire find.

sources.title: Charles Beckingham: Ibn Battuta
sources.note: Direct scholarly article read, Third visit: 1333, Samarkand ruins, riverside gardens and shrine; source criticism at opening retained through explicit attribution.

sources.title: Spyrou, Musralina and colleagues: Fourteenth-century central Eurasian plague evidence
sources.note: Direct paper read (Nature 606, 718 to 724, 2022); Figure 1d exact Sanmaq mawtana transcription/translation, infection in three individuals. Supplementary Information PDF directly read, pages 18 to 19 Qutluq Tarim jewellery and date, page 13 Sanmaq AD 1337 to 1338 range. Main paper and supplement treated as ONE work for word budget. Supplement URL https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art:10.1038%2Fs41586-022-04800-3/MediaObjects/41586_2022_4800_MOESM1_ESM.pdf .

sources.title: Gerhard Doerfer: Chaghatay language and literature
sources.note: Direct scholarly entry read: Development and Iranian linguistic influence, fifteenth-century Timurid literary centres. Linguistic category distinguished from dynasty.

sources.title: Ashmolean Museum: Silver coin HCR15902
sources.note: Direct university museum catalogue read: obverse Arabic السلطان محمود خان, separate Timur name, Samarkand mint, 802 AH / 1399 to 1400, both Timur and Mahmud Khan. Translation of title and name is literal; explicitly a Timurid-era nominal khan witness, not proof of independent Chaghatayid control.

proposedOverrides.name: Chagatai Khanate
proposedOverrides.summary: Central Asian Mongol rulers governed pasturelands and towns; western and eastern branches followed different histories after the fourteenth-century division.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Existing exact indexed identity only. Golden Horde duplicate avoided: already covered by khanate-of-the-golden-horde card and two overrides. No added aliases.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Index 1279 to 1530 circa. Inheritance from 1220s, regionally controlled civil administration from 1260s, western/eastern division from 1340s. Timurid western government from 1370; eastern Chagatai dynasties continue into seventeenth century. Map interval not a polity lifetime.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 1279/1300 same bbox [60.0252,31.7577,93.8079,50.4003]; 1400 [64.4964,34.8198,93.8079,50.4014]; 1492/1500 extend implausibly to longitude 141.2564 and latitude 57.5989. Public opening explicitly calls later eastern extension wrong. Full decoded evidence ../identity-all-snapshots.json; no geometry repair claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Sanmaq Syriac mawtana around 1338, published Roman transcription, not excavated DNA person. Second witness original Arabic script on 1399 to 1400 Ashmolean coin, explicitly western Timurid successor context and nominal Khan Mahmud, no claim of continued independent western khanate.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Chang Chun household details are 1221 formation-era background, clearly dated before separate khanate. Nature main article and supplement counted as one work. Coin-hoard museum subset distinguished from full original excavation. Older accession and religious chronologies replaced by Biran only where discussed; no assumption of uniform religious conversion.
batchIdentityNotes.override: Retain imported dates as map_coverage; fell null, successors empty until target identity/event/geometry independently verified.
